notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 3 continuous 25-ft bays, W36X247 girders, two 35-ton cab cranes, on new freestanding W14X311 columns with column caps, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 931 kN (209 kip), exceeds the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 recommendation of 222 kN (50 kip) for column brackets: the girders bear on column caps over the new crane columns (direct column bearing).

selections.designed: None: end fork on the column cap (bearing stiffeners and bolted bottom flange)
selections.reason: A girder on a column cap is held by its bearing stiffeners and bolted bottom flange (fork), the top-flange restraint of the analysis: no flange tie.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.82, vertical deflection 0.14 and lateral 0.26 of their limits; flanges at least 267 mm wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 91 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W33X241: tips ratio 0.90 > 0.85. Configurator sizing ratios; the full calculation checks the section.

New cantilever column for a 35-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 1.09 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios.

selections.designed: 1 bolted slip-critical splice: SP1 5.83 ft (0.233 L) past grid 2
selections.reason: The continuous girder exceeds the 60 ft practical shipping and erection piece: automatic placement 0.20 to 0.25 of the span from an interior support (the inflection region, nearest 0.22 L), every piece within 60 ft. A490 1 in slip-critical bolts (Class B): top flange 12 bolts each side on two inner plates 0.875 in thick, bottom flange 8 on an outer plate 0.75 in and two inner plates 0.75 in, web 18 on two plates 0.5 in; sized for the larger of the estimated factored actions at the joints (raised by 1/0.85) and 50% of the flange strength (governing: Top flange splice · plates tension rupture, 0.98).

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.) with the rail supplier's joint bars and bolts (deferred submittal), bolts pretensioned and re-tightened after 30 and 90 days of operation.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
